transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because my work actually told me I needed to come in. I do maintenance and repair, and lately, I just keep forgetting things. Like, scheduled callbacks, work orders I'm supposed to handle, or even just basic follow-ups I promised people I'd do. It’s gotten to the point where it’s all piled up on me. They basically sent me here to get it sorted out before I lose my chance at a promotion.
When did you first notice these memory problems starting to happen? Was it sudden, or did it come on gradually over weeks or months?

Well, it’s been noticeably worse for about 11 months now. I guess you could say it started really piling up then. That’s when the new management company took over and... well, they changed our whole department over to digital work orders. They also started wanting a lot stricter documentation for everything we do. Ever since that switch, I just haven't been able to keep on top of it all.

Outside of work, do you notice these memory problems affecting your personal life too — like remembering appointments, bills, or things people tell you at home — or is it mainly just the work-related stuff?

Honestly, I haven't really noticed it being a problem at home. It seems like it's mainly just the work-related stuff. I mean, my home life is pretty simple, so there's not as much to keep track of. But yeah, it's really just at the job where I'm dropping the ball.
Have you had any recent head injuries, high fevers or infections, started any new medications, or been diagnosed with any medical conditions in the past year or so?

No, nothing like that. I haven't hit my head or had any bad fevers or anything. I'm not taking any new medications, either. Honestly, I haven't been sick or diagnosed with any new medical conditions. Physically, I feel perfectly fine.
Over these past 11 months, have you noticed any changes in your mood — like feeling down, anxious, irritable, or stressed — or has it been mainly just the memory and focus problems at work?

No, my mood has been pretty normal, honestly. I haven't been feeling down or anxious or anything like that. It's really just the focus and remembering things at work that's been the issue. I mean, it's frustrating, sure, but I wouldn't say I'm stressed out or irritable because of it. Just... having a hard time keeping up with the new system.

Have you noticed any actual decline in your ability to think clearly or solve problems, or has anyone else — like family or coworkers — commented that you seem different cognitively compared to before the management change?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I can still think through things and fix problems just fine, especially when I'm working on the equipment. It's really just keeping track of all the new paperwork and procedures. And nobody has said anything to me about acting different or not thinking clearly. It's just the memory stuff with the new system.
Over these past 11 months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels — like sleeping more or less than usual, eating differently, or feeling more tired than normal?

No, not really. My sleep has been about the same as always. I eat normally, too, so I haven't noticed any changes there. And my energy is fine... I mean, I'm tired after a long shift, but just the regular amount of tired, you know? Nothing out of the ordinary.
When the new digital work order system came in, did you receive any training on how to use it, and have you been able to learn how it works, or has it been confusing to pick up?

Yeah, we had a training session when they first rolled it out. I sat through it, and I mean, I understand *how* it's supposed to work. It's not that the computer part of it is too confusing or that I can't figure out the buttons. I get the steps. It's just... doing it, keeping track of all those steps while I'm actually working, that's where I keep messing up. So I learned it, I just can't seem to stay on top of it.

If you had to learn something completely new and unrelated to work — like picking up a hobby or learning a new skill — do you find that you're able to learn and remember new information just as well as you could before, or have you noticed a change in your ability to pick up new things in general?

I haven't really noticed any change with that. If I need to learn something new outside of work, I pick it up just fine. Like, if I'm figuring out how to fix something different around the house or, I don't know, trying out a new hobby... I can learn it and remember it just like I always could. 

It really is just that new work system that's giving me grief. But my actual ability to learn things in general? No, that hasn't changed at all.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F06.8 (Other specified mental disorder due to known physiological condition). Patient has no medical conditions, head injuries, infections, medication changes, or physiological factors that would explain cognitive symptoms. The memory problems are specific to the work domain (digital system management) and do not affect general learning ability, personal life, or other cognitive domains. This is a problem of occupational adjustment/adaptation to new work procedures rather than a neuropsychiatric disorder.
